skill.name: wayfinder
skill.description: Plan work spanning many agent sessions as a shared issue-tracker map. Resolve focused investigation tickets until the route to the destination is clear.
skill.summary: Turn large, uncertain efforts into coordinated issue-tracker maps and focused decision tickets.
skill.author: mattpocock

security_audit.summary: All 13 static detections are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, fenced examples, and prose about issue identifiers. The workflow still presents moderate operational risks because it permits consequential tracker changes and may record sensitive operational metadata.

remediation.issue: The workflow permits access provisioning, data movement, and destructive tracker changes without an explicit approval gate.
remediation.suggestion: Require user confirmation before provisioning access, moving data, deleting tickets, or changing issues outside the selected map.

remediation.issue: Resolution records may include credential locations and other sensitive operational metadata.
remediation.suggestion: Store only non-sensitive references, redact restricted details, and verify tracker visibility before posting resolution comments.

content.user_title: Chart Complex Work Across Agent Sessions
content.value_statement: Large efforts lose context when they exceed one agent session. Wayfinder organizes decisions as a shared issue map that agents resolve incrementally.
actual_capabilities: Defines a clear destination and scope for a large, uncertain effort.
Creates a canonical issue map with child investigation and decision tickets.
Classifies tickets as research, prototype, grilling, or task work.
Models dependencies and identifies unblocked, unclaimed frontier tickets.
Records completed decisions as concise links while preserving detailed ticket context.
Coordinates parallel sessions through tracker assignments and one-ticket session limits.
limitations: Requires an issue tracker or a local Markdown tracker with documented operations.
Plans decisions by default and does not deliver the final implementation.
Relies on companion grilling and domain-modeling skills for guided discovery.
Handles only one ticket per session, so small efforts may not benefit.

use_cases.title: Plan a Platform Migration
use_cases.description: Map architecture decisions, research dependencies, and unresolved risks before implementation begins.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Product Discovery
use_cases.description: Organize prototypes, stakeholder questions, and scope decisions across several collaborative sessions.

use_cases.title: Structure a Research Program
use_cases.description: Track independent investigations, dependencies, and conclusions without loading every detail into each session.

prompt_templates.title: Chart a New Map
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Wayfinder to chart this effort: [idea]. Help me define the destination, scope, first frontier, and remaining uncertainty.
prompt_templates.scenario: Start a large effort from a broad idea.

prompt_templates.title: Continue an Existing Map
prompt_templates.prompt: Continue Wayfinder map [issue URL or number]. Select the first unclaimed frontier ticket, claim it, and resolve only that ticket.
prompt_templates.scenario: Resume work in a later agent session.

prompt_templates.title: Resolve a Specific Decision
prompt_templates.prompt: Open Wayfinder map [map reference] and resolve ticket [ticket name]. Consult related decisions only when needed, then update the map.
prompt_templates.scenario: Direct a session toward a known decision.

prompt_templates.title: Reconcile a Changed Route
prompt_templates.prompt: Review Wayfinder map [map reference] after [new decision]. Update dependencies, graduate newly clear questions, and remove invalidated or out-of-scope tickets.
prompt_templates.scenario: Maintain a complex map after a decision changes the plan.

output_examples.input: Chart a migration from a monolith to services.
output_examples.output: Destination: an approved migration specification. The map identifies ownership, service boundaries, data movement, rollout, and observability as linked decision areas.
Selected and claimed: Define guest checkout requirements. Resolution recorded, ticket closed, and two newly visible research questions added with dependencies.

output_examples.input: Resolve the storage decision and update the map.
output_examples.output: The decision selects managed object storage. The map now links the full rationale, unblocks retention planning, and marks self-hosting as out of scope.

best_practices: Define a measurable destination before creating tickets.
Keep each ticket focused on one decision that fits one agent session.
Use tracker assignments and native dependencies to coordinate concurrent sessions.
anti_patterns: Do not use Wayfinder when the complete effort fits one session.
Do not duplicate full ticket answers inside the map.
Do not resolve multiple tickets or begin final implementation during one planning session.

faq.question: When should I use Wayfinder?
faq.answer: Use it when uncertainty and context exceed one agent session and several decisions must be coordinated.

faq.question: Does Wayfinder implement the final solution?
faq.answer: No. It plans by default and stops when the route is clear, unless the map notes explicitly include execution.

faq.question: Which issue trackers are supported?
faq.answer: The workflow is tracker-independent, but your repository must document child issues, dependencies, claims, and frontier queries.

faq.question: Can several agents work on one map?
faq.answer: Yes. Agents claim tickets through assignments and should select only open, unblocked, unclaimed work.

faq.question: What happens when new questions appear?
faq.answer: Create precise tickets when possible. Keep unclear areas in Not yet specified until prior decisions make them actionable.

faq.question: How are completed decisions preserved?
faq.answer: Each answer remains on its closed ticket. The map adds a concise linked summary for later sessions.
